venue.name: Bailey Studio, Nanaimo Theatre Group
venue.description: Nanaimo Theatre Group is a volunteer run community theatre society, now in its 66th season, that stages its own productions in the Bailey Studio at 2373 Rosstown Road in Nanaimo. The Bailey Studio is an air conditioned 172 seat house with a lounge for refreshments, computerised lighting and modern sound, and free parking in its own lot. All areas are wheelchair accessible, there is a drop off area, and infra red hearing units are provided on request. Tickets are sold one performance at a time through the society's own online box office, and nothing on the site offers a school booking, a daycare booking or a group rate.
venue.address: The Bailey Studio, 2373 Rosstown Road, PO Box 796, Nanaimo, BC V9R 5M2

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: All areas are wheelchair accessible. There is a drop-off area for our physically challenged patrons.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Free parking is available in our well-lit lot at the Bailey Studio.

restrictions: In consideration of the actors and other patrons children must be a minimum of 3 years old to attend. (published against Humpty Dumpty, the December 2026 pantomime)
Adult Themes - Age 16+ Recommended. (published against The Birds and the Bees, September and October 2026)
venue.seasonal_notes: Their season runs from September through to the spring, with a pantomime over Christmas. The 2026 to 2027 season is The Birds and the Bees from 20 September to 10 October 2026, Humpty Dumpty from 18 to 31 December 2026, and The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee from 21 February to 13 March 2027. Tickets for the season went on sale 23 August 2026.

programs.name: Christmas pantomime, public performance
programs.description: Each December the society stages a family pantomime in the Bailey Studio. The 2026 one is Humpty Dumpty, written and directed by Ann Gogo with music director Liam Pister, running 18 to 31 December 2026, in which Dame Candy Kain and her son Justin rally the people of Lower Danceville in song and dance against a greedy chief executive. The page carries a firm minimum age: children must be at least 3 years old to attend. Seats are reserved and numbered, and tickets are bought one at a time through their online box office. No group rate, school rate or block booking is published, and no ticket price appears anywhere on their own website.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in a numbered seat in a small 172 seat theatre and watch a live pantomime with songs and dancing. Refreshments can be had in the lounge.
programs.our_note: The minimum age of 3 is the only firm age rule they publish, and it is worth reading as a real one rather than a suggestion. Seats are reserved, so if you want a class sitting together you need to buy the block yourself in one go on their ticketing site. Ring the ticket line on 250-758-7224 and ask whether they will hold a row and whether there is any rate for a group, because neither is on the site.
programs.practical_summary: Free parking in their own lot, a lounge for refreshments, step free access throughout and a drop off area. Washrooms, somewhere to eat a packed lunch and room for a bus are not mentioned anywhere, and no ticket price is published on their site.
programs.extra_fees_note: No ticket price is published anywhere on the theatre's own website. Prices appear only once you pick a seat in their online box office.
programs.evidence: In consideration of the actors and other patrons children must be a minimum of 3 years old to attend.

programs.name: Mainstage play or musical, public performance

Age guidance is set per production and printed on the season page rather than as a house rule: The Birds and the Bees, running 20 September to 10 October 2026, carries 'Adult Themes - Age 16+ Recommended', while The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee, 21 February to 13 March 2027, is described as including audience participation. Seats are reserved and bought one at a time through their online box office. No group rate, school rate or block booking is published, and no ticket price appears on their own website.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in a numbered seat in a small 172 seat theatre and watch a live play or musical. Refreshments can be had in the lounge.
programs.our_note: Read the age line on each show before you commit, because it changes from production to production and this season opens with one recommended for 16 and over. Seats are reserved, so a class sitting together means buying the block yourself in one transaction. Nothing on their site is set up for a school or a daycare, so start with a phone call to the ticket line.

Washrooms, lunch space and bus parking are not mentioned, no ticket price is published on their site, and the age guidance depends on which show you pick.

gaps: Nothing on this site is bookable by a school or a daycare as a group. There is no schools page, no education page, no group rate, no block booking form and no matinee set aside for classes. Tickets are bought one seat at a time through their online box office. The page at /groups sounds promising but it is a Wix members discussion feed for cast and crew, not group bookings.

There is no youth programme and no theatre school. The only workshops on the site are technical, stagecraft and acting workshops that are free to members, with dates set once enough people sign up, and membership is $25 a year for an adult or $40 for a family. Children can take part in productions: if a cast member is under 16 only a $5 performance fee is charged.

No ticket price of any kind is published on the theatre's own website. Prices only appear inside their online box office once a performance and a seat have been chosen, so nothing has been recorded here.
Whether they host school or daycare groups is not addressed anywhere on the site, so both fields are null rather than false.
Washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site, and neither is anywhere to eat a packed lunch. The lounge is described only for refreshments.
Bus parking is not addressed. The site says only that there is free parking in their own well lit lot.
Stroller access is not addressed. Wheelchair access is, and the site says all areas are accessible with a drop off area, plus infra red hearing units on request.

Performance start times are published only on their ticketing site, per date, not on their own pages, so no time slots have been recorded. The calendar there currently shows 14:00 matinees and 19:30 evenings for the September run.
Duration of a performance is not published.

Capacity is not recorded. The site gives the size of the room, an intimate 172 seat house, but says nothing about how many seats one party may book, so that number sits in the description rather than as a booking limit.
The costume and prop rental mentioned on their community page is offered to individuals and other theatre groups, not as a children's activity, so it has not been recorded as a programme.
Alt text for all four photographs was written after opening each image in a browser and looking at it. None of them carries alt text on the page.
The og:image on the home page is not a photograph, so the header photo here was taken from the Our Studio row on their about page instead.

BROWSER NOTE: the four Our Studio photographs on the about page are lazy loaded and report no dimensions until they scroll into view, and the map on the contact page only draws after the page has been scrolled. A plain fetch sees neither.

The site is built on Wix and publishes its own business location coordinates, 49.1956911 and -124.0017596, against the address 2373 Rosstown Rd, Nanaimo. Recorded to five decimal places. An independent lookup of the same street address returns Bailey Studio at 49.1956857, -124.0016579, about eight metres away, so the published point is the building and not a map centre.
